# Evaluating LLM Applications

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/evaluating-llm-applications)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/evaluating-llm-applications/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/evaluating-llm-applications) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-evaluating-llm-applications/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-evaluating-llm-applications/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

Know whether an LLM application works, and whether a change made it better: test sets, checks, judges you can trust and statistics that hold up, on a documentation assistant for a small command-line tool.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For engineers who have shipped, or are about to ship, a feature built on a model: an assistant, a question-answering service or an extraction step. They write Python and know prompts, embeddings and tests, but not statistics beyond a mean.

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12.15
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python list-the-docs.py
```

The examples load an open model, pinned to an exact commit with every file's SHA-256 in `examples/models.toml`: [Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B/tree/c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca). The first run downloads it from Hugging Face (about 1,449 MB); after that, the examples run offline.

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a hosted model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

Where the data comes from, and its licence: [`examples/data/docs/README.md`](examples/data/docs/README.md), [`examples/data/gsm8k/README.md`](examples/data/gsm8k/README.md), [`examples/data/helpsteer2/README.md`](examples/data/helpsteer2/README.md), [`examples/data/truthfulqa/README.md`](examples/data/truthfulqa/README.md).

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, the examples that use it run again in the new version, and every example runs again each week. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/evaluating-llm-applications/changes).

## Contribute
